context_requirements: Expression of dopamine receptors (DRD2/DRD3) or other targets such as HTR2A, HRH1, ADRA1A
Intact downstream signaling through AKT/STAT3/NF-kB for antiproliferative and apoptotic effects
Proliferative drive that can be inhibited (e.g., hormone receptor-positive or other oncogenic signaling)
TP53 wild-type or functional for robust apoptotic and cell-cycle arrest responses
falsifiers: No change in any of the proximal immediate-early genes (FOS, EGR1, JUN) at 6 h in any cell line
No reduction in proliferation markers (e.g., CCNA2, CCNB1, MKI67) at 24 h in any cell line
No induction of apoptosis or cell-cycle arrest markers (e.g., CDKN1A, PMAIP1) at 24 h
Strong and consistent upregulation of proliferation genes across all lines at 24 h
Lack of any transcriptional response (all genes unchanged) in all nine cell lines at both time points

evidence.supports: Thioridazine, a dopamine receptor antagonist, inhibits tumor growth and induces apoptosis in breast cancer models, with effects on AKT/STAT3/NF-kB signaling.
D2 dopamine receptor blockade induces immediate-early genes (c-fos, zif268) in striatal neurons, demonstrating transcriptional response to DR antagonists.
